Panasonic air conditioners have been developed to provide outstanding comfort, starting with the first room air conditioner in 1958. Over the years, they have introduced various innovations, including the first room heater/air conditioner in 1972, an air conditioner with a human detection sensor in 1993, and models with nanoe™ technology in 2008. The company, founded in 1918 by Konosuke Matsushita, has evolved to include air conditioners with ECONAVI. Panasonic Corporation, formerly Matsushita Electric Industrial Co., Ltd., changed its name in 2008 to align with its global brand name. The company operates through segments including Lifestyle, which offers air-conditioners among other products.

These products are designed for energy efficiency and can operate in extreme temperatures ranging from +52°C to -25°C. Features include voice control, Wi-Fi control, and air purification. The company has been a leader in the industry since 1958, providing innovative and reliable air conditioning units. Panasonic's AC pricing model includes a range of price points from entry-level to premium, with 45% of its current business coming from its smart range. The company emphasizes premiumization while maintaining affordability through consumer finance options. Revenue streams for Panasonic's HVAC & CC division are shifting towards a recurring-revenue model focused on Machines In the Field (MIF), which includes post-hardware sales services and engineering. Additionally, Panasonic is expanding its Indian AC hub, aiming to increase its exposure to South Asia's Consumer Durables demand, although profit margins are currently at 2.6%, lower than last year.

The key term here is Machines In the Field (MIF)—the company’s own equipment and facilities installed and running at customer sites. HVAC & CC places strong emphasis on its MIF as “stock” assets and plans to turn it into a source of recurring revenue. Instead of a “flow” model that earns revenue by selling equipment to new customers, the company is shifting to a recurring-revenue model. Under this approach, the company draws on that “stock” advantage to broaden its range of services and [...] Aiming for further business growth, HVAC & CC will expand its recurring-revenue business—centered on MIF and including service and engineering—and shift toward a revenue model that earns through post hardware sales services and engineering. By maintaining relationships with customers after hardware is sold, the company will strengthen both the stability and the growth potential of its revenue. On using MIF as a driving force for expansion, Katayama notes that this strategy has also been jointly [...] Katayama acknowledges that combining the heating and ventilation A/C business with the cold chain business is rare, even when looking worldwide, and far from easy. The aim of this reorganization and integration is to strengthen competitiveness in the highly competitive heating and ventilation A/C business by using revenue from profitable, non-competitive areas as a source of capital to support growth.

In 2025, Panasonic Corporation announced the release of the OASYS Residential Central Air Conditioning System in the US market, featuring a Mini Split AC, ERV, and transfer fans using DC motor-driven ventilation fans. The company also launched the X-Premium Inverter Series in Malaysia, a next-generation 2-in-1 smart air conditioning solution. In 2026, Panasonic's AC model saw improvements such as higher ISEER efficiency, lower yearly power consumption, a new DustBuster outdoor self-clean feature, and an 8-in-1 convertible mode. The 2026 model also had a refreshed outdoor unit design and retained the same cooling capacity, room coverage, filter, app support, condenser, and warranty structure as the 2025 model.

According to reviews on All Cool Sales, many customers are happy with Panasonic’s energy-efficient air conditioners, particularly the Econavi series, which saves on electricity bills. Customers also appreciate the durability, smart device control, and quiet operation of Panasonic air conditioners. However, on Pissed Consumer and Trustpilot, Panasonic has low ratings of 1.7 and 1.4 stars respectively, with many customers citing dissatisfaction with customer service, defective products, and issues with warranty handling. While some customers praise product performance, the majority express significant concerns about the brand's service and product quality.

Many are happy with Panasonic’s energy-efficient air conditioners. The Econavi series, for example, saves on electricity bills. Customers like controlling their ACs with smart devices. This shows Panasonic’s dedication to improving products and making customers happy since 1958.
